Since \(B=\frac{13}{12}W\), we have \(B-W=\frac{W}{12}\). Checkerboard counts differ by at most 1, and \(B>W\), so \(B-W=1\). Thus \(W=12\), \(B=13\), and total pieces \(nm=25\).

For a chocolate bar with more than one row and column, the only factor pair is \(5\times 5\), so
\[
m+n=5+5=10.
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
